description_en: Two stone pillars erected on the west side of the main road to Dailekh Bazar. The two pillars gave its name to the locality, Duikhambā (two pillars), located a few hundred meters south of Dailekh Bazar. The pillars are set in cemented bases, directly on the side of the road.Both pillars are oriented east-west, altough, as is often the case with this type of objects, they were displaced from their original location.Eroded inscriptions are present on the east face of the north pillar and on the west face of the south pillar.Stone pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th century. They are installed to honor the memory of deceased persons, mostly warriors. The Duīkhambā pillars are datable to the early 15th century. They are mentioned inAndolfatto 2019,Pokharel 2011: 77 and inSharma 2012: 127-128.
references: REFERENCES Pokharel, Bishwo K. C. Kīrtikhamba . Kathmandu: Prakāśka, 2011. Sharma, Dilli Raj. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies, 2012. Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019.

historical_events.event_description: On the western face of the southern pillar (DLK0020-002) is a very eroded inscription composed of four or five lines, in Devanāgarī script.According to D. R.Sharmathe inscription reads: 'tra de wa naṃ śuvamastu'.

On the eastern face of the northern pillar (DLK0020-001) is a very eroded inscription composed of six lines, in Devanāgarī script.According to D. R.Sharmathe inscription reads: 'Oṁ swosti sāke 1331 bhādra badi... kirti'
